title: Diadora Offers $40,000 NIL for High School Sub-4
excerpt: Diadora offered $40,000 NIL deals to the first high schoolers to run sub-4:00 (boys) or sub-4:35 (girls) in its spikes. Weighing gear incentives.
body:
Diadora and the retailer Marathon Sports offered a $40,000 NIL deal to the first US high school boy to run a sub-4:00 mile, and the first girl to run sub-4:35, while wearing Diadora's Mezzofondo spike during the 2025–26 indoor season (December 8, 2025 to March 15, 2026). Athletes had to race exclusively in the Mezzofondo, under-18s needed parental consent, and deals had to comply with state association, school and NCAA rules. Diadora says the spike returns about 4% more energy than other leading distance spikes, a figure from its own testing.

Offers like this tie a reward to a specific piece of equipment. For young athletes in particular, the decision is worth thinking through: the right spike is the one that fits and suits your event, not the one with the biggest prize attached.

Whether you're a high school athlete or an adult considering a brand deal, first ask whether the gear or commitment serves your training. Equipment should follow what you need to perform, not the other way around.

Sources: Marathon Sports; LetsRun.com
keyTakeaway: Choose gear and commitments because they help your training, not because of the reward attached.
